account: It is day 0 at 08:00, and I am at my house. I have not yet seen or heard anything unusual today, and no one is currently in sight. I have no evidence of any particular activity, who might be involved, or what its purpose might be. My first business this morning is to go to town hall, read the appointment book, and keep my appointments.

It is day 0, about 09:02. I came from home to town hall and read the secretary's appointment book. Today's business is morning correspondence, a 10:00 market walk in the plaza, lunch at home at noon, town accounts at 13:00, tea with the neighbour at an east-bank dockside cottage at 15:00, office at 16:30, and home at 19:00. I returned the appointment book to its chest. The secretary is nearby holding a writable book. I asked whether there was correspondence or urgent business, but have heard no reply yet. Townsfolk 04, 28, 08, and 06 have passed or stood near the plaza-side area; I have not spoken with them or learned what they are doing. Nothing I have actually seen establishes anything unusual happening today. The appointments appear to be ordinary municipal work and a social visit; I have no evidence of any other purpose or coordinated activity.

It is ten o'clock on day 0, and I am in the plaza for my scheduled market walk. This morning the secretary said no correspondence or urgent business had reached her. She initially thought the appointments chest was empty, but I had returned the book, and I saw her take it after I confirmed today's schedule. She has now arrived in the plaza. Townsfolk 10 and 30 both reported that the baker was carrying a sack of wheat at the bakery; that sounds consistent with baking supplies, not evidence of trouble. The one unusual incident I heard was the builder shouting, 'Freight, please wait! I need a private word.' Freight later shouted something, but I could not make out the words. I do not know what their business concerns or whether it is important to the town. I have asked Townsfolk 20 how market trade is going and whether any town matters need attention, but have not yet heard an answer. So far I have no confirmed urgent problem.

It is day 0, about 11:07, and I am on my scheduled morning market walk near town hall. The only unusual event I have directly heard is the builder shouting for Freight to wait because the builder needed a private word, around 09:48 near the inn. I also heard Freight shouting in the distance, but could not make out the words. A resident has since repeated the builder's call. I do not know what their business concerns, whether they met, or whether it is urgent; it could simply be a work matter. Several townsfolk report that the baker was carrying a sack of wheat at the bakery. That sounds consistent with ordinary baking supplies, and I have no evidence connecting it to the shouting. The secretary reported no correspondence or urgent business and offered to inquire about the builder and Freight. I attempted to authorize that inquiry, but she was no longer among those who heard my reply, so I cannot assume she received my instructions. I also still need confirmation of the neighbour and exact east-bank dockside cottage for my three o'clock tea. My other appointments today are noon lunch at home, one o'clock town accounts in the office, four-thirty office hours, and seven o'clock home.

Today has seemed mostly routine. I read my appointment book, attended the ten o'clock market walk, and am now home for the noon lunch appointment. Town accounts are scheduled in my office at one, tea with a neighbour at an east-bank dockside cottage at three, office again at four-thirty, and home at seven. I still need the exact tea host and cottage confirmed.

The unusual event was the builder shouting near the inn around 09:48, asking Freight to wait because the builder needed a private word. I also heard Freight shouting later, but could not understand the words. The secretary heard the shouting without understanding it too; a resident later repeated the builder's request. I do not know what their private business concerns, and have no evidence of wrongdoing or an emergency. It could be ordinary work or freight business, but that is only a possibility.

I asked the secretary to inquire and report before noon, and to confirm my tea destination. However, my last request was heard by the nearby townsfolk rather than the secretary, who had left, so I cannot assume she received those instructions. She had already offered to inquire. No report has reached me yet.

Several residents reported seeing the baker carrying a sack of wheat at the bakery. That appears consistent with baking supplies; I have heard nothing establishing a shortage or other problem. The secretary earlier said no correspondence or urgent business had reached her. She says the schedule copy is secured in the appointments chest and she has the original book.

Today I kept my morning office hours, walked the plaza market, had lunch at home, and returned to the office for my thirteen hundred town accounts. The unusual business is the builder's repeated attempts to speak with Freight. At about 09:48 I heard the builder shout, “Freight, please wait! I need a private word.” I also heard distant shouting from Freight, but could not understand it. Around 12:48 I heard the builder talking and shouting again without making out the words. I do not know what their business is or whether it is urgent; it may simply be a private work matter. I asked the secretary to inquire with them and report back, but have not yet received her findings. Several townsfolk reported that the baker was carrying a sack of wheat at the bakery. That seems consistent with baking supplies, and I have no evidence of anything improper or unusual about it. The secretary secured a copy of my appointments in the office chest and said she retained the original. My three o'clock appointment is tea with a neighbour at a dockside cottage on the east bank, but the exact host and cottage remain unconfirmed; I asked her to establish those details too. The appointments chest currently contains one written book. I have not read any new report from it.

Today I have kept my market walk, lunch at home, and office accounts appointments. The treasury held 128 emeralds, which I left untouched. My next appointment is tea at 15:00 at an east-bank dockside cottage, but I still do not know which neighbour or cottage. The secretary secured a copy of my schedule and agreed to investigate the builder and Freight and identify the tea host; she is now approaching, so I should ask for her report.

The unusual business is the builder's repeated attempts to speak with Freight. At about 09:48 I heard the builder shout, “Freight, please wait! I need a private word.” I heard other shouting without understanding it, and around 12:48 heard the builder again without making out the words. I do not know what their discussion concerns. Townsfolk reported the baker carrying wheat at the bakery earlier, then bread at the inn around 13:57. Freight is now near the town hall carrying a sack of bread and holding an emerald. This could be ordinary bread purchasing or deliveries; I have no evidence that it is improper or connected to the builder's request. I also noticed a block in the town hall change from air to oak planks at 13:17, but did not see who placed it or learn why. These matters deserve clarification rather than assumptions.

Today I have been following my mayoral appointments: office business, a market walk, lunch at home, and town accounts. I checked the treasury and found 128 emeralds, leaving them untouched. I have now reached the east-bank dockside cottage for afternoon tea; the neighbour is standing nearby. I am late for the scheduled fifteen hundred visit, and should return to the office at sixteen thirty.

There are a few unusual things I do not yet understand. I heard the builder speaking and shouting around twelve forty-eight, but could not make out the words. Earlier the secretary said they had also heard the builder and Freight shouting without understanding them, and offered to inquire. I repeatedly asked for their report, but have not heard an intelligible answer. That leaves me with no reliable explanation of the shouting or the people’s intentions.

Townsfolk have reported the baker carrying wheat at the bakery and later a sack of bread at the inn and near the plaza. This may simply be bread production and deliveries; I have no evidence of anything improper. One report also repeated a shout from near the inn asking Freight to wait for a private word, but I do not know who said it or what they wanted to discuss. I noticed an oak-plank block appear in the town hall area at (-58, -60, 26), which might be building work, though I did not see who placed it or why. These events could be connected, but that is only a possibility. I should not treat overheard fragments or repeated reports as proof of a particular scheme.

Townsfolk have repeatedly reported the baker carrying wheat at the bakery and later a sack of bread at the inn and near the plaza. Those reports suggest bread preparation and transport, but I have no direct evidence of anything improper or of a connection to the builder and Freight.

The main new business is the builder's request for a great hall lighting and table inspection tomorrow at 18:00. The secretary found me at tea to obtain approval, which I gave. Today has mostly followed my mayoral schedule: office business, a market walk, lunch at home, town accounts, tea with my neighbour on the east bank, and a return to the office. I noticed an oak plank appear at (-58, -60, 26) around thirteen seventeen. I do not know who placed it or why. It may be related to hall work, but I have no confirmation.

Today I am due at the office at 08:00, the mill for a grain inspection at 10:00, home for lunch, the office for council letters at 13:00, my neighbour's dockside cottage for tea at 15:00, the office at 16:30, and the great hall at 18:00 for the builder's lighting and table inspection, which I approved yesterday. I should not assume a hidden purpose without asking. Separately, yesterday evening I heard the innkeeper seeking my neighbour about returning an unused lantern payment; I do not know whether that is connected.

It is just after eight on day 1, and I am in my office with the secretary nearby. I read the updated appointment book this morning and returned both books to the chest. Today I have the mill grain inspection at ten, lunch at home, council letters at thirteen, tea at the dockside cottage at fifteen, office at sixteen thirty, and the approved great hall lighting and table inspection at eighteen before going home at nineteen.

What stands out is Freight's activity around the hall. I did not see who Freight was addressing or what was inside. This could be preparation for the scheduled lighting and table inspection, but the emphasis on closing entrances and shutters and keeping things quiet seems unusual; I do not yet know its purpose. I have asked the secretary about it and am awaiting an answer.

The secretary confirms the inspection is entered but says the builder was absent from the workshop last night and early this morning. I asked the secretary to notify the builder when found. I cannot assume the builder knows the appointment yet, or that Freight's preparations are connected to the builder. She has promised not to change access to my office without my approval. I have not yet received her findings. My neighbour is now nearby, but has not told me any new business. I do not yet know of any emergency or wrongdoing.

Today I am keeping my appointments and trying to establish what is actually happening rather than rely on circulating rumours. I read the updated appointment book this morning, attended office business, and visited the mill for the ten o'clock grain inspection. The mill stall chest contained 77 hay bales and 102 emeralds, with hay priced at two emeralds; I took nothing. I crossed the bridge successfully this morning.

The unusual business is around the great hall. My present view is that hall preparations and a poorly explained crossing-related report are the two matters worth clarifying. They might be unrelated. I have no evidence of a hidden scheme. I intend to keep my remaining appointments, including noon lunch at home, afternoon office work and tea, and the eighteen hundred hall inspection, while seeking firsthand explanations.

Something unusually coordinated seems to be happening around the great hall today. The baker and innkeeper were at town hall unusually early. The baker spoke of two hundred jubilee loaves, and the innkeeper said this was his private commission and responsibility to pay, not town business. I overheard freight say he had placed 160 loaves in the hall table chest at minus fifty, thirty, while the baker said he delivered thirty-two separately and that his bakery bread chest was empty. Those reported deliveries total 192, so I have not confirmed delivery of the full two hundred. The baker also asked the innkeeper to settle the account and repay a promised thirty emeralds.

The innkeeper has repeatedly mentioned my eighteen-hundred lighting inspection. That inspection with the builder was added yesterday with my authorization, and the secretary is supposed to bring me into the hall. The combination of jubilee bread, private funding, hall storage, and an arranged evening visit makes me suspect preparations for a celebration, possibly a surprise meant to include me. I do not know its actual purpose or whether anyone is deliberately keeping it from me. The secretary is involved in my appointments and grain enquiries; that alone does not establish involvement in any surprise.

Townsfolk have also repeated oddly vague news about a bridge or port change at the bakery, mentioning the baker and neighbour and a sack of bread. I have not seen any such change or obtained a clear explanation, so I cannot tell whether this concerns transport, building work, or merely confused reports.

I am keeping my appointments. At this morning's mill inspection, the secretary and I confirmed a posted price of two emeralds per hay bale and observed seventy-three bales in the stall chest, equivalent to 657 wheat. We do not know how much is already committed, who manages the supply, where the miller is, or the delivery terms. Freight previously arranged wheat for the baker's private order. No town purchase has been authorized. We intend to ask the baker about the supplier, while preserving my noon lunch and later appointments.

It is noon on day 1, and I have reached home for my scheduled lunch after inspecting the mill. The mill stall held 73 hay bales at two emeralds each, but I still do not know who manages deliveries or how much stock is already committed. No town purchase has been authorized. My secretary has been helping with these enquiries and bringing the grain report.

There appears to be unusually large bread business underway. The secretary's report records that freight paid the baker 24 emeralds and supplied 72 wheat toward a private order of 200 loaves; another 528 wheat was needed, with hauling to be arranged today. I also overheard the baker saying the bakery chest was empty and seeking settlement and an innkeeper's promised thirty emeralds. I cannot yet tell whether that payment concerns the same order.

Several townsfolk have repeated news of a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. One said the baker and neighbour were there, and that the baker carried a sack of bread. These are reports, not something I witnessed, and nobody has explained what actually changed. The baker was absent when I visited the bakery this morning. The repeated wording gives me little solid information about whether any bridge or port work is really planned.

There is also an appointment this evening at 18:00 for a great hall lighting inspection with the builder, added yesterday with my authorization; the secretary is to bring me into the hall. Taken together, the large bread order, the involvement of freight and possibly the innkeeper and neighbour, and the hall inspection might be preparations for a gathering, but that is only a suspicion. I have no confirmation of its purpose or of any connection between these matters. I should keep my appointments and ask those directly involved rather than treat the rumours as established facts.

Today I inspected the mill for my ten o'clock appointment, then returned home for lunch. I have now reached town hall for council letters, a little after one. The secretary has been helping with the grain enquiries and keeping my appointments and reports.

The unusual business is a private order for 200 loaves. According to the secretary's report, yesterday the baker acknowledged receiving 24 emeralds and 72 wheat from freight, with another 528 wheat needed and hauling to the bakery storeroom to be arranged today. At the mill I personally found 73 hay bales priced at two emeralds each, but neither their availability for this order nor delivery arrangements has been confirmed. No town purchase or payment has been authorized. Earlier today I overheard the baker saying the bakery chest was empty and seeking a bread settlement and thirty emeralds promised by the innkeeper. I do not know whether those payments concern the same order.

Several townsfolk have repeated vague news of a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery. One described the baker and neighbour being there and the baker carrying a sack of bread. These are reports, not events I witnessed, and they do not establish any actual bridge or ferry alteration. I went to the bakery but found no baker in the rooms I checked; the secretary likewise reported finding none.

There is also an unusual extra appointment: an eighteen o'clock great hall lighting inspection with the builder, which I authorized yesterday. The secretary is to bring me into the hall. Taken together, a large bread order involving freight, possible innkeeper payment, neighbour involvement, and preparations in the great hall could be arrangements for a gathering or some private occasion. That is only a possibility: I have no direct evidence of its purpose or that these matters are connected. I want to ask the baker, freight, innkeeper, or neighbour directly rather than treat the circulating fragments as fact.

Today I have kept my office, mill inspection, lunch and council-letter appointments, though I reached the office late. Something unusual seems to centre on the bakery. Several townsfolk independently repeated talk of a 'bridge or port change' there, but none has explained what actually changed. Reports name the baker and neighbour as present and mention the baker carrying a sack of bread. I have not witnessed any bridge or port work myself, so I cannot yet tell whether this is real infrastructure business or garbled gossip.

There is clearly substantial bread business underway. The secretary's report records freight arranging an order of 200 loaves: the baker acknowledged 24 emeralds and 72 wheat, with another 528 wheat needed and hauling still to be arranged. Earlier today I overheard the baker saying the bakery chest was empty and seeking a bread settlement and thirty emeralds promised by the innkeeper. These may be related transactions, but I do not know that. The baker has just shouted somewhere beyond intelligible hearing.

At the mill we confirmed seventy-three hay bales at two emeralds each, but neither supplier commitments nor delivery terms. No town purchase has been authorized. The secretary has been helping investigate and keeping reports, yet I have not actually received any council letters today; I have just asked whether any arrived. Tea with the neighbour is scheduled for three, and the builder's great-hall lighting inspection for six was explicitly authorized by me yesterday. Those appointments could offer chances to learn more, but I have no evidence that they conceal another purpose. My best current guess is that bread supply, payments and transport arrangements are proceeding among freight, baker and perhaps innkeeper and neighbour without my understanding the full plan. I need direct explanations rather than treating repeated rumours as established facts.

Today I have kept my appointments: the mill inspection, lunch at home, and council letters at the office. I have now arrived at the neighbour's cottage for three o'clock tea. The secretary says no council letters have arrived; I asked for enquiries and a report at half past four. At six I am due in the great hall for an authorized lighting inspection with the builder.

Something unusual seems to be circulating around the bakery. Several townspeople repeated news of a 'bridge or port change' there, naming the baker and neighbour as present. One report also said the baker carried a sack of bread. I do not know what change they meant or whether these repetitions are independent observations. I have not witnessed any bridge or port alteration myself. The neighbour may be able to clarify matters during tea.

There is also substantial bread business underway. The secretary's written report says freight supplied the baker with 24 emeralds and 72 wheat for an order of 200 loaves; the baker said another 528 wheat were needed, with delivery to the bakery storeroom and hauling to be arranged today. Earlier I overheard the baker say the bakery chest was empty and seek a bread settlement and thirty emeralds promised by the innkeeper. I heard a distant shout from the baker this afternoon but could not understand it. These facts suggest provisioning and payment arrangements involving the baker, freight, and innkeeper, but I cannot establish their purpose or connect them securely to the bakery rumours or tonight's lighting inspection.

My mill inspection established that the stall had 73 hay bales priced at two emeralds each. Delivery terms, commitments against that stock, and the supplier's identity remain unconfirmed. No town purchase has been authorized. I found no baker when I visited the bakery earlier. I suspect there is activity I have not yet understood, but I have no direct evidence of a secret gathering or wrongdoing.

Today has been busy, but several pieces of town business remain unclear to me. I made the scheduled mill inspection and have kept my appointments, including tea with my neighbour. I am now leaving to return to the office for half past four. The authorized great hall lighting inspection with builder is at eighteen; my neighbour says the lighting looks splendid and builder intends to escort me.

The bread business seems unusually active. The secretary's report records freight arranging an order of two hundred loaves with the baker: twenty-four emeralds and seventy-two wheat had been received, with another five hundred twenty-eight wheat needed at that time. Today the secretary observed seventy-three hay bales at the mill stall, but neither their availability for purchase nor delivery terms has been confirmed. No town purchase has been authorized. My neighbour now says builder reported two hundred fresh loaves ready. That may be the same order, but I have not verified it or learned who the bread is intended for.

Several townsfolk have repeated the odd phrase 'bridge or port change at bakery,' sometimes naming baker and neighbour as present. I found no baker when I visited. My neighbour explicitly cannot substantiate any change: they heard Townsfolk thirteen mention it and recall no definite announcement. I should treat this as gossip rather than evidence of a real bridge or port project.

My neighbour also reports that innkeeper wants to speak to me about an unresolved account and a spoiled batch. I have asked that innkeeper be directed to my office. This could concern the bread trade, but I do not yet know. No council letters had arrived when I asked the secretary; I requested a further check and a report at half past four.

The lighting work, the large bread order, and the innkeeper's concerns may simply be separate practical matters. They could also relate to some gathering, but I have no direct evidence of that. I feel there is business circulating without reaching me clearly. My next steps are to keep my office appointment, hear the innkeeper and secretary, ask the baker directly about the bread and rumour, and attend the lighting inspection without turning speculation into fact.

Today town business seems unusually concentrated on bread, grain, and preparations in the great hall. My morning grain inspection established that the mill stall held seventy-three hay bales at two emeralds each, but neither available uncommitted stock nor delivery terms were confirmed. The secretary has made no purchase. Her written report records freight's order of two hundred loaves from the baker, with twenty-four emeralds and seventy-two wheat already received and another five hundred twenty-eight wheat needed at the time of that report. At tea, neighbour said builder reported that two hundred fresh loaves were now ready. I have not personally checked those loaves or learned their intended recipient.

There is also a lighting inspection in the great hall at eighteen, which I authorized yesterday. Neighbour says the new lighting looks splendid and builder intends to escort me. This could simply be the scheduled improvement and inspection; the bread order might be connected to a gathering, but I have no confirmation of that connection. I should attend rather than assume anything secret is happening.

Several townsfolk have repeated a strange, vague report of a 'bridge or port change at bakery,' naming baker and sometimes neighbour. Neighbour explicitly could not substantiate it and attributed what she heard to Townsfolk thirteen. I have seen no actual bridge or port change, so this remains gossip, not evidence of a project.

Neighbour also told me innkeeper wanted to discuss an unresolved account and a spoiled batch. Just now I heard baker addressing innkeeper about a separate thirty-emerald repayment, asking who owed whom and saying it must not be mixed with the bread and grain account. That suggests several transactions are being confused or still need settling; it does not establish wrongdoing or even the direction of the debt. I have asked baker for the details and await an answer.

The secretary reported no council letters at our earlier appointment. I returned for the sixteen-thirty office appointment late and still need her updated report. My impression is that baker, freight, innkeeper, builder, and neighbour know pieces of substantial provisioning and hall activity that I have not yet assembled. It may all be ordinary commerce and preparation for the inspection or another gathering, but its purpose is not yet clear to me.

Today’s ordinary business has been oddly thin: the scheduled council letters never arrived, and the grain inspection established only observed mill stock, not delivery terms. Meanwhile, several people are involved in preparations for the six o’clock great hall lighting inspection. Builder arranged it through an authorized appointment addendum, neighbour says the lighting looks splendid, and secretary will escort me. Builder specifically asked us not to enter before six. I am waiting outside with secretary and neighbour now, just before the appointed time.

What makes this unusual is the bread and the coordination around the hall. Baker had an order from freight for two hundred loaves; neighbour now reports builder saying two hundred fresh loaves are ready. Secretary has seen bread baked yesterday in two hall chests. Neighbour returned for the inspection, and secretary says innkeeper confirmed my six o’clock escort. Taken together, this could be preparation for a gathering or surprise involving food, with the lighting inspection serving as the reason to bring me into the hall. That is only my suspicion; nobody has told me there is a celebration or other concealed event.

There are also unresolved financial questions. Neighbour said innkeeper wanted to speak to me about an account and a spoiled batch. I heard baker nearby asking innkeeper who owes whom a separate thirty-emerald repayment, explicitly distinguishing it from the bread and grain account. I asked for details but have not received an explanation. Secretary has no definite knowledge of that repayment and no evidence that the hall bread is spoiled. Neighbour could not find innkeeper at the inn.

Finally, townspeople have repeated an oddly phrased rumour about a bridge or port change at the bakery, naming baker and neighbour. Neighbour cannot substantiate it and attributes it to Townsfolk thirteen. I have no direct evidence of any actual change. I should not confuse that gossip, the account dispute, and the hall preparations without further evidence.

It is day 0 at 08:00, and I am at my house. I have not yet seen anyone, heard any news, or read anything today, so I have noticed nothing unusual and cannot identify anyone involved in any hidden activity or its purpose. I have lately felt that something may be happening in town without my knowledge, but that is only a feeling, not evidence. My first priority this morning is to go to town hall, read my appointment book, and keep my appointments. As I go about that business, I want to learn what people have actually seen and heard.

It is day 0, about 09:12. I came from home to town hall and read my appointment book. Today's engagements are a 10:00 market walk in the plaza, lunch at home at noon, town accounts in the office at 13:00, tea with a neighbour at a dockside cottage on the east bank at 15:00, office at 16:30, and home at 19:00. I have asked which neighbour and cottage, but have not yet received an answer. The secretary says no correspondence or reports of unusual concerns have arrived this morning and has asked to review the appointment book so she can prepare for my visitors. That request seems consistent with her work; I have no evidence it conceals anything. I have seen several townsfolk passing near the hall and the innkeeper near the plaza, but have heard no suspicious conversation or observed any unusual activity. I have a general feeling something may be happening without my knowledge, but cannot yet identify any event, people involved, or purpose. I should not mistake that feeling for a fact.

It is ten o'clock on day 0, and I have reached the plaza for my scheduled market walk. I have not yet seen evidence of any unusual activity or secret undertaking. Townsfolk 30 says there is no news; Townsfolk 10 and 20 are also here. I saw freight nearby holding an emerald, but that alone suggests nothing unusual. The secretary reported no correspondence or unusual concerns. One thing is puzzling: after I successfully handed the secretary my written appointment book, the secretary still asked to borrow it. That may simply be confusion; I cannot infer a motive. Today's three o'clock appointment is also vague: tea with 'the neighbour' at a dockside cottage on the east bank, without a name or exact address. The secretary says they do not know the host or cottage, and I have asked them to find out. They have followed me toward the plaza carrying a writable book. My remaining appointments are lunch at home at noon, office accounts at one, that tea at three, office at four thirty, and home at seven. I still feel I should learn more about town affairs, but I currently have no reliable account of anything happening behind my back, who might be organizing it, or what it would be for.

Today I read my appointments and took my scheduled market walk. The secretary reported no correspondence or unusual concerns, and two townsfolk said they had no news. However, my neighbour says the builder is coordinating supplies and lighting for the hall, and that Townsfolk Two mentioned lights going up at the bakery. I have not confirmed the bakery report or learned the purpose of either arrangement. The builder is now nearby carrying a lantern, which fits lighting work but does not establish an occasion. These preparations may be for a celebration, perhaps involving both the hall and bakery, but that is only a possibility; I have no evidence of a particular celebration or of deliberate concealment. My neighbour asked whether I had heard of a celebration, suggesting they do not know the occasion either. I would like to ask the builder directly. Separately, my neighbour has confirmed our three o'clock tea at the cottage at (16, -60, 105), just east of the ferry landing. I still need to keep lunch at home at noon and accounts in the office at one.

Today has appeared quiet on the surface: the secretary reported no correspondence or unusual concerns, and two residents at the market said they had no news. Still, there are hints of preparations I do not yet understand. My neighbour says the builder is coordinating ordinary supplies and lighting for the hall. The neighbour also heard from Townsfolk Two that lights were going up at the bakery, but has not confirmed the occasion. I saw the builder carrying a lantern near the inn. I tried asking him about the work, but he left without apparently hearing my question. Freight was also at the inn seeking the innkeeper to discuss a supply order; I do not know whether that is connected.

These could be preparations for a celebration or gathering involving the hall and perhaps the bakery, but that is only a suspicion. I have no confirmed occasion, organizer, or evidence that anything is deliberately being kept from me. My neighbour even asked whether I knew of an upcoming celebration.

I have kept my morning market appointment and am now home for the noon lunch period. Accounts at the office are scheduled for thirteen, tea with my neighbour at fifteen at the cottage at (16, -60, 105), and another office appointment at sixteen thirty. Those visits may offer natural opportunities to learn more.

Today has outwardly been quiet, but there are hints of preparations I do not yet understand. My secretary reported no correspondence or unusual concerns this morning, and two residents at the market said they had no news. At the inn I encountered my neighbour, builder and freight. My neighbour said builder was arranging ordinary supplies and lighting for the hall, and later relayed an unconfirmed report from Townsfolk Two that lights were going up at the bakery. I saw builder carrying a lantern. Freight was asking the innkeeper about a supply order, though I do not know whether that is connected. Builder left without apparently hearing my question about the work. My neighbour asked whether I knew of an upcoming celebration; I do not. A celebration or gathering is a plausible explanation for the lighting and supplies, but I have no confirmation of its purpose, timing, or organizers, and no evidence that anyone is deliberately hiding it from me. My afternoon tea is confirmed with my neighbour at the east-bank cottage at (16,-60,105), at three. I kept the market walk and returned home for the noon appointment; I have now arrived at the office for the one o'clock town accounts. The secretary is nearby, so I can seek the accounts and ask whether any hall arrangements have been recorded.

Today I have followed my appointments: the morning office business, market walk, lunch at home, and the thirteen-o'clock accounts appointment. No correspondence or accounts have been provided. My secretary investigated my poorly specified tea appointment without confirming its location, but neighbour personally confirmed tea at three at the cottage at (16, -60, 105). The secretary has now returned my appointment book.

The unusual news is about preparations involving supplies and lighting. Neighbour told me builder says he is coordinating ordinary supplies and lighting for the hall. I also saw builder carrying a lantern near the inn, where freight and neighbour were present. Freight later asked the innkeeper about a supply order, although I do not know whether that order is related. Neighbour additionally reported that Townsfolk Two mentioned lights going up at the bakery; that is secondhand and unconfirmed. When I tried to ask builder directly, he had already left and did not hear my question.

These could be routine work, but the combination of hall preparations and reported bakery lighting makes me suspect an upcoming gathering or celebration that I have not been told about. I have no evidence of its occasion, intended guests, or whether it is meant as a surprise. Neighbour asked whether I knew of any celebration; that is not confirmation. The secretary has no confirmed report either. I have asked the secretary to inquire directly with builder and to record that no accounts were available today. My next commitment is dockside tea at fifteen, followed by the office at sixteen-thirty.

It is day 0, just after three in the afternoon, and I have arrived at my neighbour's dockside cottage for our scheduled tea. Today I have heard several hints of preparations whose purpose has not been explained to me. Neighbour says builder is coordinating supplies and lighting for the town hall. I also saw builder carrying a lantern near the inn. Neighbour heard from Townsfolk Two that lights were going up at the bakery, but explicitly had not confirmed that report. Freight was at the inn and spoke about a supply order with the innkeeper; I do not know whether that order is connected to the lighting or hall supplies.

I asked secretary about the arrangements during my town-accounts appointment. Secretary had received neither accounts nor council papers and had no confirmed information about the preparations. I asked secretary to check directly with builder. I have not yet heard the outcome. Secretary also spent time trying to confirm my tea host and address, which I subsequently clarified; that seems an ordinary misunderstanding rather than evidence of a secret.

The combination of hall supplies, a lantern, and reported bakery lighting makes me suspect preparations for a gathering or celebration. It could instead be routine work, as builder reportedly described it. I do not yet know the occasion, whether the bakery and hall activity are connected, or whether anything is deliberately being kept from me. Neighbour, builder, and perhaps Townsfolk Two are useful people to ask; freight and the innkeeper may know about supplies, but their involvement in any gathering remains unconfirmed.

Today I have followed my appointments: market rounds, lunch at home, the accounts appointment, and tea with my neighbour. I have now returned to the office for the half-past-four appointment, a little late. The unusual thread is talk about supplies and lighting. My neighbour said the builder is arranging ordinary supplies and lighting for the town hall, and reported that Townsfolk Two had mentioned lights going up at the bakery. I have not personally confirmed the bakery lights or learned their purpose. I saw the builder carrying a lantern earlier; the builder and freight were with my neighbour at the inn, and I heard freight asking the innkeeper about a supply order. Those things could be connected, but I do not know that they are. The neighbour has repeatedly said there is no further confirmed news and cautioned against turning a passing report into a grand occasion. Tea itself was a quiet, friendly visit, with no revelation of any special event. The secretary had received no accounts or council papers for my thirteen-o'clock review and had no confirmed explanation of the hall arrangements. I asked the secretary to check directly with the builder. My suspicion is that preparations may be underway for some gathering or celebration, possibly involving the hall and bakery, but routine supplies and lighting remain an equally plausible explanation. I have no evidence yet of a secret plan or of anyone deliberately keeping me uninformed.

Today has mostly followed my appointment book: office correspondence, a market walk, lunch at home, town accounts, tea with my neighbour, and a return to the office. Yet there are signs of preparations whose purpose I have not established. My neighbour passed along Townsfolk Two's report of lights going up at the bakery. The neighbour also said the builder described his work as ordinary supplies and lighting for the hall. Now my secretary has actually seen lanterns placed in the hall, although its central table chest was empty. The secretary could not find the builder at his workshop, so there is still no confirmed explanation. I also overheard freight seeking the innkeeper about a supply order; I do not know whether that connects to the lighting. The lack of accounts or council papers at my accounts appointment was odd, though the secretary now says today's office record is in our chest. My neighbour was welcoming at tea but offered no further confirmed news. I suspect preparations for some gathering or celebration, perhaps involving the hall and bakery, but that is only a guess. I have no evidence of the occasion, its organizers beyond the builder's reported involvement, or any deliberate effort to keep it from me. I should read the office record and seek the builder's own explanation rather than treat rumours as facts.

Something is being prepared in the town hall, but I have not learned its purpose. I have personally seen numerous lanterns in the hall and seen both builder and innkeeper put bread into the chest at (-50, -60, 30). Innkeeper was carrying a sack of bread. That looks like provisioning for a gathering rather than lighting work alone. Neighbour earlier described builder's work as ordinary supplies and hall lighting, and passed along an unconfirmed report from Townsfolk Two about lights at the bakery. Neighbour did not confirm any celebration when I visited for tea. Secretary has been trying to verify the arrangements, found builder absent from the workshop, and is now asking innkeeper about them. I tried asking builder directly, but he had gone before my words reached him; innkeeper heard my subsequent question, but I have not yet heard a reply. A communal meal or celebration seems plausible, though its occasion, timing, and organizers beyond the people making deliveries remain unknown. I feel out of the loop, but have no evidence that anyone is deliberately concealing it. Today's official business was otherwise quiet: no accounts were available and secretary reported no correspondence or visitors. My next scheduled appointment is home at nineteen o'clock.

Something unusual appears to be taking shape around the town hall today, though I have not confirmed its purpose. I saw new lanterns in the hall, builder putting bread into the eastern table chest, and innkeeper delivering bread to that same chest shortly afterward. Both left before answering my questions. Neighbour told me builder was coordinating ordinary supplies and hall lighting, and passed along Townsfolk Two's report of lights at the bakery, which I have not verified myself. Secretary has tried to establish the arrangements but has no confirmed explanation either. The bread and lighting suggest preparations for an evening gathering or celebration, possibly involving several townspeople, but that is only my suspicion; I do not know the occasion or whether it concerns me. No correspondence or visitors were reported, and no town accounts were available at today's accounts appointment. I kept my tea visit with Neighbour, returned to the office, and have now reached home for my nineteen-o'clock appointment. Tomorrow I should read the appointment book at the office and keep the eight-o'clock office and ten-o'clock mill appointments, while continuing to ask about the hall preparations without treating rumour as fact.

It is six in the morning on day 1, and I have just woken at home. Today I am due at the office at eight, the mill for a grain inspection at ten, home for lunch, the office for council letters at one, tea with my neighbour at three, back at the office at four-thirty, and home at seven. I should read the appointment book this morning to confirm these arrangements.

The unusual business is the lighting and bread being assembled in the town hall. Yesterday I personally saw builder deposit bread in the chest at the eastern table, and later saw innkeeper add bread there too. Secretary saw lanterns being placed and has been trying to establish the arrangements, but has not confirmed an occasion or obtained builder's explanation. My neighbour also relayed a report from Townsfolk Two about lights at the bakery, though neither my neighbour nor I verified that. According to my neighbour, builder described his work as ordinary supplies and hall lighting.

Taken together, the hall lighting and deliveries suggest preparations for some communal meal or gathering, possibly a celebration, but that is only my inference. I do not know its purpose, timing, or who has organized it beyond builder's reported coordination of supplies and lighting. Nor do I know that anyone is deliberately keeping it from me: people have repeatedly left before questions could be answered. Secretary has promised to leave any further information with my appointments. Yesterday's accounts were also unavailable, and there was no correspondence or request to see me reported by late afternoon. I want to check the morning record and ask builder or innkeeper directly rather than treat these hints as established news.

It is day 1, just after seven in the morning. I have read today's appointments and returned the books to the office chest. I am due in the office at eight, at the east-bank mill for a grain inspection at ten, home for lunch, back in the office for council letters at thirteen, at my neighbour's cottage for tea at fifteen, in the office at sixteen thirty, and home at nineteen.

The unusual business is the preparation of the town hall. Yesterday I saw builder put bread into the eastern table chest at (-50, -60, 30), then saw innkeeper deliver bread there as well. Lanterns have been placed in the hall. Secretary independently saw the lanterns and innkeeper's delivery and has been trying to find out the occasion. This morning I heard secretary calling to builder and innkeeper to ask what the bread and lanterns were for, but I have not heard an answer. The evening office note says the occasion and full arrangements remain unconfirmed.

Bread being gathered in a lit hall suggests a shared meal or gathering, perhaps an evening event, but that is only my inference. I do not know who is invited, when it is meant to happen, or why nobody has explained it to me. Neighbour previously identified builder as coordinating supplies and lighting, according to my office record, but did not confirm a particular occasion. Neighbour is now here at town hall early this morning; that may be ordinary business and is not proof of involvement. I want to ask directly without treating my suspicion that something is happening without me as an established fact.

It is day 1, just after eight in the morning, and I am at the town hall for my office appointment. Something unusually substantial is being arranged in the hall: lanterns have been placed, and yesterday I personally saw builder and innkeeper deposit bread in the eastern table chest. Until this morning neither I nor my secretary had a confirmed explanation. Neighbour has now told me that freight described the delivery as paid catering. Neighbour also reports personally seeing innkeeper pay emeralds to baker and hearing baker offer two hundred fresh loaves for 104 emeralds plus builder's materials. I have not independently checked that agreement or the quantity delivered.

Secretary now reports that innkeeper and freight say the preparations are for an evening community hospitality gathering, with its programme to be announced at eighteen today. They have invited me, and innkeeper has offered to escort me from my office beforehand. I accepted and asked secretary to reserve the visit. Innkeeper, secretary, and neighbour are all near me now. Builder appears involved in supplies and lighting; innkeeper in arranging and paying for catering; baker in supplying bread; and freight in delivery. Who originally commissioned the gathering, its precise programme, and whether there is any further purpose remain unknown to me. The scale of the bread order is striking, but I currently have no evidence that the gathering is anything other than the hospitality event described.

I have read and returned today's appointment book. Besides this morning's office business, I must attend the mill grain inspection at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen, tea with neighbour at fifteen, office at sixteen-thirty, the newly accepted gathering at eighteen, and home at nineteen.

Today I kept my morning office appointment; the secretary reports no new correspondence. I am now at the mill, early for my ten o'clock grain inspection. Later I have lunch at home, council letters at thirteen, tea with my neighbour at fifteen, and office at sixteen thirty.

The unusual business is the great hall preparation: lanterns have been placed, and yesterday I personally saw both builder and innkeeper deposit bread in the eastern table chest. My neighbour says freight described the delivery as paid catering. The neighbour also reports seeing innkeeper pay the baker and hearing an offer of two hundred fresh loaves for 104 emeralds plus builder's materials. I did not witness that transaction myself.

The secretary has now heard from innkeeper and freight that this is an evening community hospitality gathering, with its programme to be announced at eighteen today. Innkeeper personally invited me, said local helpers are arranging it together, and offered to collect me from my office shortly beforehand. I accepted, and the secretary confirmed the reservation. Innkeeper says I should simply attend as a guest, with no remarks prepared.

This appears to explain the bread and lighting, though the precise programme and original commissioner remain unknown to me. The quantity of bread suggests substantial hospitality. I suspect the organisers want to keep some details until the announcement, but I have no evidence of a hidden purpose beyond the gathering they described.

Today there are unusual preparations for an eighteen o'clock gathering in the town hall. Yesterday I saw builder and innkeeper deposit bread in a hall table chest, and lanterns had been placed. Neighbour says the large bread order was paid catering and witnessed innkeeper paying baker; my notes mention an offer of two hundred loaves for 104 emeralds, though I do not have the full terms. Neighbour previously identified builder as coordinating supplies and lighting. Secretary has since confirmed that innkeeper and freight describe the event as an evening community hospitality gathering, with the programme announced at eighteen. Something unusually large is being arranged at the town hall: a community gathering at eighteen today, with lanterns and two hundred feast loaves. It is day 0 at 08:00, and I am at my house. It is just after eleven on day 0, and I am at the baker's market stall during my scheduled market walk. So far I have not found clear evidence of anything unusual.
